notes.title: Revisiting the SpaceX Valuation: A Post-Prospectus Update!
notes.text: Values enterprise value at $1.22 trillion and equity at $1.3 trillion, about $100 a share (the equity rises mostly from $75 billion of IPO cash). 2025 revenue grew about one-third (connectivity almost 50%, AI about 22%, space 7.64%); 2025 operating loss $2.57 billion, net loss about $5 billion. Raised AI target revenue from $80 billion to $160 billion but cut its target margin from 45% to 25%; space target margin 45%; connectivity 60%. Cost of capital 8.37% at the start and 8.25% in steady state. Book equity $41.3 billion, debt including leases $22.9 billion, cash $24.7 billion, 12,535 million shares. Calls the reported $28 trillion total addressable market "fantasy." An offering price near $135 a share (about $1.8 trillion) is "too richly priced" against his $1.25-$1.35 trillion range: overvalued at the rumored price. Main risk is AI overreach, magnified by Musk's more than 85% voting control.

notes.title: The Anthropic Feedback Loop: The Cost of Capital Delusion and Diversion!
notes.text: Values equity at about $1.45 trillion, down from an earlier $1.475 trillion after adding leaked third-quarter numbers. Uses a 9.74% cost of capital, a BB+ rating for debt and a 10% failure risk. Base case: revenue near $100 billion over the next twelve months and about $1 trillion in ten years, target operating margin 32.5%. Calls the governance structure (public benefit corporation, founder-controlled voting shares) a "red flag." Compute commitments total just over $450 billion (present value about $373 billion); cash $114 billion, above $200 billion after the IPO. No value per share: bankers will adjust the share count.

notes.title: The Anthropic Prospectus Arrives: My (but not the) IPO valuation!
notes.text: Equity value $1.475 trillion, at the low end of the $1.5-$2 trillion offer range; he would sit out if it priced well above his $1.48 trillion. Inputs: revenue about $1 trillion by 2036, pre-tax operating margin 32.5% (cut to 27.5% for regulatory drag), $1 of reinvestment per $3 of new revenue, 9.74% cost of capital (US median 9.16%), 10% failure probability. Facts: first-half revenue about 14x the prior year, operating loss above $8 billion before adjustments, $80 billion reported loss including a $72 billion non-cash charge, compute costs down from over 250% to 48% of quarterly revenue. His worst case is -$373 billion and best case $4.04 trillion; calls both extremes "possible, but unlikely."

notes.title: A Golden Year (2025): Gold's Price Surge - The Signal in the Noise!
notes.text: Overpriced on historical metrics: $4,118/oz on Oct 24, 2025, up 57% year to date and up from $1,060 at the end of 2015. Gold/CPI ratio 17.81 vs medians of 2.93 (1963-2024) and 3.77 (1971-2024); his regression implies about 3.19. Gold/silver ratio 84.73 vs a historical median of 57.09. Stocks compounded 11.38% a year from 1984-2024 vs 5.35% for gold. Gold ETFs eased access and added to demand. Demand-side shifts explain the rise.

notes.text: Look reasonably valued on P/E but quite expensive on price to free cash flow. Companies now need about 5x the capital to grow a dollar of sales versus a decade ago, so ROIC is falling as capex rises. Low confidence in the returns on the capex; expects cuts eventually. He plans to stay on the sidelines.

notes.title: Contrarian Low-Cost Producer at a 15% FCF Yield + Excess Real Estate
notes.text: His main pick. Low-cost producer with about 60% share in its region and natural barriers to competition. 15% FCF yield (6.8x FCF), healthy balance sheet, uses free cash flow for buybacks, and benefits from new legislation effective Jan 1, 2026. After the Berry deal, about $80 a share of proven reserves (PV-10) against a $43 stock price. Also has excess real estate and a "call option" on extra revenue streams. Long-life, low-decline production versus shale.

notes.title: Weekend Thoughts: Malone's Born to Be Wired Book; Thoughts on Cable; Is CHTR Cheap?
notes.text: Has never owned it. About $126 a share, roughly 4x free cash flow (about $31 per share last year). Management plans to cut capex from about $11.5B to $8B, which he doubts is sustainable. Buying Cox; his napkin math puts combined FCF near $64 a share, about 50% of market cap. About $100B of debt, so it trades like a call option on revenue stability. Down 42% in ten years. He stays on the sidelines. Starlink and Amazon Leo (up to 1 Gbps) are potential threats to cable broadband.
